results.title: United States Government to Reinstate Section 301 Import Tariffs on Artificial Graphite from China - NOVONIX
results.content: — NOVONIX Limited (NASDAQ: NVX, ASX: NVX) (“NOVONIX”), a leading battery materials and technology company, today applauded the recent announcement by the United States Trade Representative (USTR) on Section 301 tariffs, removing the current exclusions and reimposing the 25% tariff on artificial graphite and natural graphite powder imported from China effective June 15, 2024.1 In addition, USTR previously announced new tariffs on natural flake graphite on May 14, 2024, increasing to 25% in [...] to 25% in 2026.2 [...] Dr. Chris Burns, CEO of NOVONIX, said, “We are pleased to see the Biden Administration and the USTR formally recognize the significance of the Section 301 tariffs to protect the investments being made by companies like NOVONIX. Employing this trade tool will help to level an otherwise disparate playing field and support our efforts to localize the production of battery-grade graphite.”

results.title: New Section 301 Tariffs Take Effect | Brewers Association
results.content:
On July 23, the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) finalized new Section 301 tariffs covering most goods from 60 economies. The new duties took effect at 12:01 a.m. E.D.T. on July 24, immediately after a temporary 150-day 10% global import surcharge imposed in February expired. For many brewery-related imports, tariff costs will remain near their previous level, although Australian and New Zealand hops and many types of Chinese equipment now face a higher 12.5% rate. results.content:
1. List 1 ($34B): 25% tariff on 818 HTS codes including industrial machinery, auto parts, and chemicals. Effective July 2018.
2. List 2 ($16B): 25% tariff on 279 HTS codes including semiconductors, plastics, and motorcycles. Effective August 2018.
3. List 3 ($200B): 25% tariff on approximately 5,700 HTS codes covering a broad range of consumer and industrial goods. Effective September 2018, raised from 10% to 25% in May 2019. Semiconductor tariffs increased from 25% to 50%. Lithium-ion EV battery tariffs increased to 25% (effective 2026). Steel and aluminum tariffs increased to 25%. These increases reflect the administration’s strategic focus on protecting domestic manufacturing in critical technology sectors. [...] Key 2026 change
